findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: There were no signed employee health reporting agreements available in the facility. The owner stated that they moved them to their off-site office. Paperwork that is required for health inspections should stay in the facility to be viewed at every inspection. A follow up is scheduled for 8/25/2026 to ensure that there are signed employee health reporting agreements available for every employee.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: The facility did not have a Norovirus cleanup policy available. CORRECTED- The inspector provided a written policy and the facility possesses bleach to effectively complete the procedure. Ensure that there is always a vomit and diarrhea clean-up policy in the facility at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The handwashing sink in the dish room area was observed to have multiple dishes in it. CORRECTED- The PIC removed all dishes from the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for their intended purpose of handwashing and that they are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

findings.comment: All of the handwashing sinks, the preparation sink, and the triple sink are observed to need to be sealed to the wall. There is a gap between the wall and each of the sinks. Ensure that these sinks are sealed to the wall and the sealing is made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
There were no food handler certificates available to view in the facility for any of the employees. The owner stated that they moved them to their off-site office. All paperwork that is required for health inspections should stay at the facility to be viewed at each inspection. Ensure that food handler cards are available in the facility for all staff and that all staff have completed their food handler training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) who has their Allergen Awareness training. This was discussed with the CFPM, who stated that they will work on obtaining their allergen training. Ensure that there is always a CFPM who has completed their Allergen Awareness training in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The hand-sink in the dish room area was obstructed with a container holding various items. Discussed that all hand-sinks must remain unobstructed to allow employees to wash hands. Be sure to educate employees on never placing items in sink because it can interfere with proper handwashing. Ensure that hand sinks remain unobstructed.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The soap dispenser at the bar’s handwashing sink was observed empty. A bag of soap was replaced by the PIC to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are supplied with hand-soap to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The chemical dish washing machine was tested at 0ppm (CL). The machine was primed and still tested at an improper concentration. The facility removed all of the buckets associated with mechanical ware washing, including detergent, rinse, and sanitizer because they were empty. The quaternary ammonium dispenser at the triple sink was also observed empty. The facility uses quat tablets for their sanitizer buckets. The facility was instructed to create a sanitizer solution at the triple sink with the tablets until the chlorine chemical arrives (later today) for the dish machine. The sanitizing chemical arrived in the midst of the inspection and was tested at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that the dish machine is always testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A bean sauce placed on an ice bath was probed at 71F. The PIC indicated that the sauce was recently placed on ice but most of the ice was observed melted.The PIC was shown how to properly create an ice bath, where the ice level matched the food level. As ice melts, be sure that more ice is added to maintain cold temperatures. Ensure that ice baths are sufficient to maintain a temperature of 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Various sauces are placed on ice baths throughout the facility. A bean sauce was probed at 71F. The kitchen manager indicated that the sauce was recently placed on ice. Most of the ice was observed melted and at improper cold holding temperatures. The manager was instructed to add more ice to the container to ensure that all outer areas of the containers are covered with ice. Ensure that all TCS foods held on ice baths are kept at a temperature of 41F or less to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There weren’t any sanitizer buckets present in the kitchen area, despite the facility being in full operation. Sani solutions were prepared and placed at each station to correct the violation. All buckets were tested between 200ppm - 400ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are always available if food is being prepared, handled, and served.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The chlorine test strips that the facility has available are completely soiled. Discussed with both the owner and the kitchen manager that test strips shall be in good condition to accurately test sanitizer concentration. A container of CL test strips were given to the owner to correct the violation. Ensure that test strips are always available to accurately measure sanitizing concentrations.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: There was a mop bucket that contained waste water stored inside of the waste room. The PIC indicated that facility usually dumps water outdoors. Educated the employee that dumping waste water outdoors on the ground is prohibited and to immediately stop the activity. There is a mop sink that is available for proper disposal inside of the facility. Instructed the facility to ALWAYS use the mop sink for waste water disposal.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.11 Approved Sewage Disposal System. SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant; or (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is about a half inch gap in between the sink and the wall located in the food prep room. Shown to the PIC. Ensure that the handsink is sealed to the wall to prevent accumulated food debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

(C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a pan of pork and Queso to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, both item ware prepped this week, correct date marks were placed on products. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours has the proper date marking available.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).
